newsitem.title: LEBANON: Peace talks must be based on land-for-peace, Poos.
newsitem.headline: Peace talks must be based on land-for-peace, Poos.

text.p: Luxembourg's Foreign Minister Jacques Poos said in Beirut on Friday that Israel's stalled peace talks with Lebanon and Syria should resume on the basis of the land-for-peace formula.

"I assured my counterpart that all the European Union countries think a final solution should be based on international law as set by the United Nations and the principle of land-for-peace," Poos said after talks with Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez.
"If our Israeli friends accept this principle then the negotiations can be possible over the ways, the security assurances and schedules," added Poos.
The Israeli-Syrian and Lebanese-Syrian talks are stalled over the issue of an Israeli withdrawal from the Golan Heights and in south Lebanon.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ousted moderate Shimon Peres last May on a platform rejecting trading peace for occupied Arab land -- a formula laid at the 1991 Madrid peace conference.
Poos, who is preparing to take over the EU presidency in July, hailed the Israeli-PLO Hebron deal as a step forward in a long process.
"We see that this deal should be followed by other stages and it should not be an end point in the Palestinian-Israeli negotiations," Poos added.

Bouez, whose country has in the past attacked the PLO for signing a separate peace deal with Israel in 1993, said the deal extending Palestinian self-rule to Hebron did not mean that the Palestinians and Arabs have regained all their lost rights.
